title: Child and Adolescent Psychopathology
tagline: Knowing the storms by name, and the lighthouse too.
welcome: Psychopathology is not a list of defects; it is a map of sufferings, each with a path. This course teaches you to know every storm by name, and the lighthouse too.
vignette: A bright eleven-year-old begins hearing a voice that critiques him. His parents are terrified. The clinician must differentiate, explain, and act, with knowledge that is precise and a manner that is calm. Psychopathology, taught well, is mercy with a map.
vignette_attr: A first-episode presentation, drawn from practice
description: An advanced study of the onset, presentation, and course of mental disorders in childhood and adolescence: neurodevelopmental, anxiety, depressive, bipolar, trauma-related, disruptive, eating, and emerging personality pathology, with comorbidity, etiology, and treatment pathways.
questions: How does this disorder present differently in a child than an adult?
What is the interplay of biology, development, and environment?
What is the evidence-informed pathway for this young person?
importance: Early recognition and pathway to care change lifelong outcomes
Comorbidity is the rule in youth; clinicians must see complexity
Accurate formulation prevents years of mismatched treatment
misconceptions: that childhood disorders are adult disorders in miniature, when they are developmental presentations
that diagnosis is destiny, when early intervention rewrites trajectories
figures: the father of modern child psychiatry
whose developmental psychopathology integrated the field
settings: child and adolescent mental health services
outcomes: You will present each disorder as it appears across ages.
You will weigh genetic, neuro, and environmental factors.
You will see complexity without losing clarity.
You will write coherent, multi-level formulations.
You will know treatment and referral routes for each disorder.
You will explain disorders with accuracy and hope.
modules: The framework organizes everything that follows.
The most common referrals, understood deeply.
Anxiety wears many masks in childhood.
Mood disorders in youth demand careful, urgent skill.
The emerging severe disorders need earliest eyes.
assessment: Assessment tests formulation and differential skill.
tips: Always plot the disorder on the developmental timeline
Practice explaining each disorder in hopeful, honest language
integration: Psychopathology is the clinical backbone linking assessment, crisis, and treatment courses.
faith: We name the storms with compassion, believing no young person is their diagnosis.
closing: May your knowledge be precise and your hope contagious, and may every storm you name find its lighthouse.
